audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer level chart disagreed with the content layer on four rows (phases[2],[3],[4],[6] vs win[2],[3],[4],[6]) and phases[4].why described Azir winning while the side said Sylas.
audit.why: Packet levelChart (Sylas,Sylas,Sylas,Sylas,Azir,Skill,Azir) matches the content win[] row-for-row and matches the whys[]; the full layer is the stale copy. Sylas out-trades pre-6 because Kingslayer (W, 12/10.5/9/7.5/6s) heals off champion hits at 400 range while Azir has no lockdown until Emperor's Divide.
audit.corrected: Full layer moved to Sylas for L3 and L4-5, Azir for L6 and 2+ items; whys rewritten to match the verdict.

audit.why: Spikes are accurate: Sylas peaks L6 with Hijack (80/55/30s), Azir inflects at Nashor's Tooth and again at Rabadon's. Sylas's R cooldown falling to 30s at rank 3 is the reason his late-game threat never fully disappears.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no cooldown number at all (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT), and the decisive interactions were never stated: Abduct is the recast of Abscond (E, 13/12/11/10/9s) and is the only way he crosses soldier range, while Emperor's Divide is terrain that shoves him back out.
audit.why: Kit file gives Abscond/Abduct 13/12/11/10/9s, Kingslayer 12/10.5/9/7.5/6s, Chain Lash 10/9/8/7/6s, Hijack 80/55/30s, Azir E 22/20.5/19/17.5/16s. Those numbers make the advice actionable.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns field, both Do's/Don'ts bodies and enemyWin now carry real numbers and the real interaction.

audit.why: missingInteractions flags needs-antiheal for Kingslayer sustain; report[8] already instructs adding anti-heal early into his sustain, so the interaction is on the page.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was the tradeBad string verbatim, under unrelated titles (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED).
audit.why: The titles promise wave/roam advice; the bodies explained trading.
audit.corrected: Both bodies rewritten to match their titles, grounded in Sylas's waveclear and Hijack cooldown.

edits.before: E completes the safety net — you now have the shield-dash out. Greedier soldier placements are allowed, not encouraged.
edits.after: Shifting Sands completes the safety net, but his Q-E-W chain still out-trades you inside 400 range. Hold E as the escape, not the poke.

edits.before: Nashor's components arrive and the soldier DPS starts to sting. Drag Qs through Sylas on every last-hit he takes.
edits.after: Kingslayer is a heal-lunge every 7.5s and his all-in peaks — drag Qs through him on last-hits, but never stand for the answer.

edits.before: - Sylas Abscond / Abduct: matchup-defining — Dash into chain-stun — punish him hard while it is down. Check it before every step-up. - E Shifting Sands is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Abscond / Abduct: 13s at rank 1, 9s maxed — the whole lane runs on it, so step up only inside that window. - Kingslayer heals him every 12s early and 6s maxed; chip is wasted before it. - Your E is 22s at rank 1 — the escape, never the poke.

edits.before: Dash into chain-stun — punish him hard while it is down. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: Abscond is 13s at rank 1 — bait it with a soldier, count it, then step up while it is down.

edits.before: W behind the wave, Q-drag the soldier through Sylas on his last-hit, auto once through the soldier, step back — two-second trades he cannot answer without overextending.
edits.after: Sylas has no fast waveclear pre-6, so a crashed wave forces him to walk into sand or give up the plate. Ping the moment he leaves and crash the next wave too.

edits.before: That’s Sylas’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Shifting Sands is 22s at rank 1 — spend it on damage and his Abduct pull is free.

edits.before: Standing at max soldier range admiring your poke with E on cooldown — that is the engage window every Sylas player is waiting for.
edits.after: Hijack is a 950-range steal on an 80-second cooldown at rank 1, and an unpinged roam is how he funds it — track him, ping, and shove so leaving costs him the wave.

edits.before: Sylas wins by landing Abscond / Abduct, denying your pattern, and turning your every misstep into the all-in you hadn’t budgeted.
edits.after: Sylas wins by landing Abduct through your soldiers, healing the poke straight back with Kingslayer, and then casting your own Emperor's Divide at you.

edits.before: Carry through siege control — soldiers take plates, R denies engages, and your DPS curve outlasts every assassin spike in the lobby.
edits.after: Carry through range — soldiers take plates while he has to close to 400 for Kingslayer, and Emperor's Divide throws his Abduct commit back out of the fight.

edits.before: If Sylas opens the score, reset expectations and respect Abscond / Abduct doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm at soldier range and stay relevant through wave control.
edits.after: If Sylas takes a lead his Kingslayer heal makes every skirmish sustainable for him, so stop contesting: farm at soldier range, hold E purely as the escape, and let Nashor's put you back in it.

notes: Level chart: content win[2]/win[3] already read "Sylas", win[4]/win[6] already read "Azir" and match the packet levelChart and the whys[]; only the full layer was stale, so no paired content-layer edit exists to propose (the target values are already on disk). This resolves four pre-existing cross-layer disagreements rather than introducing any. Anti-heal for Kingslayer is already stated in report[8], so no new edit was needed for the missingInteractions entry.
